Computer and Information Systems Managers

About the Role
Plan, direct, or coordinate activities in such fields as electronic data processing, information systems, systems analysis, and computer programming.
What You'll Do
Direct daily operations of department, analyzing workflow, establishing priorities, developing standards and setting deadlines.
Meet with department heads, managers, supervisors, vendors, and others, to solicit cooperation and resolve problems.
Review project plans to plan and coordinate project activity.
Assign and review the work of systems analysts, programmers, and other computer-related workers.
Provide users with technical support for computer problems.
Develop computer information resources, providing for data security and control, strategic computing, and disaster recovery.
Recruit, hire, train and supervise staff, or participate in staffing decisions.
Stay abreast of advances in technology.
Consult with users, management, vendors, and technicians to assess computing needs and system requirements.
Develop and interpret organizational goals, policies, and procedures.


Tools & Technology
Customer relationship management CRM software: ACT! Premium
Desktop publishing software: Adobe Distiller
Web platform development software: Adobe Flex, Apache Tomcat
Object or component oriented development software: Advanced business application programming ABAP
Data base management system software: Alpha Four, Apache Cassandra, Apache Hadoop, Apache Pig, Apache Solr
Data base user interface and query software: Amazon Web Services AWS software
Portal server software: Apache HTTP Server
Development environment software: Apache Maven
Video creation and editing software: Apple Final Cut Pro, Apple iMovie
Presentation software: Apple iWork Keynote
Spreadsheet software: Apple iWork Numbers
Word processing software: Apple iWork Pages
Operating system software: Apple macOS
Content workflow software: Atlassian JIRA
Education & Experience
Education: Bachelor's degree or Some college, no degree
On-the-Job Training: 6 months to 1 year
Related Work Experience: 6 years to 8 years
Work Environment
E-Mail
Work With or Contribute to a Work Group or Team
Determine Tasks, Priorities and Goals
Face-to-Face Discussions with Individuals and Within Teams
Spend Time Sitting
Contact With Others
Coordinate or Lead Others in Accomplishing Work Activities
Work Outcomes and Results of Other Workers
Telephone Conversations
Freedom to Make Decisions
